what-is-an-evergreen-fund.title: What Is an Evergreen Fund?
what-is-an-evergreen-fund.meta_description: An evergreen fund is a permanent-capital investment vehicle with no fixed end date, offering periodic liquidity instead of a one-time exit. Learn how it works, its costs, and how it compares to other fund structures.
what-is-an-evergreen-fund.direct_answer: An evergreen fund is a fund structure with no set termination date, designed to hold investments indefinitely rather than winding down after a fixed term. Instead of returning capital at a predetermined exit, it offers investors periodic liquidity windows, often quarterly, while continuing to raise and deploy capital on an ongoing basis.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: Traditional private funds have a life cycle. They raise capital, invest it over several years, then sell assets and return proceeds to investors within a set window, often ten to twelve years.

An evergreen fund skips that cycle. It accepts new capital on an ongoing basis and reinvests proceeds from matured or sold positions rather than distributing everything back to investors. This lets the fund keep operating and investing indefinitely, without a mandated wind-down.

sections.heading: Liquidity
paragraphs: Evergreen funds typically offer redemption windows, often monthly or quarterly, rather than daily liquidity like a mutual fund or ETF.

Redemptions are usually capped as a percentage of fund assets during any given period. In periods of high redemption demand, an investor may not receive the full amount requested right away, since the fund is not required to sell assets to meet every request.

sections.heading: Costs and Minimums
paragraphs: Fee structures vary, but evergreen funds commonly charge a management fee and, in many cases, a performance-based fee on gains.

Minimums have come down compared to traditional private funds, which has made this structure accessible to a broader set of investors, though minimums still tend to be higher than public mutual funds or ETFs.

sections.heading: Risks to Understand
paragraphs: The underlying assets in an evergreen fund are often illiquid or infrequently priced, which means the fund's stated value may lag what the assets could actually sell for in the market.

Because redemptions are limited and can be gated, an investor should plan to hold the investment for a meaningful period. This structure is not a substitute for cash reserves or assets an investor may need to access on short notice.

faq.question: How is an evergreen fund different from a mutual fund?
faq.answer: A mutual fund offers daily liquidity because it typically holds publicly traded securities that can be sold quickly. An evergreen fund holds less liquid assets and offers redemptions only periodically, which is a structural tradeoff, not simply a smaller version of a mutual fund.

faq.question: Can I lose access to my money in an evergreen fund?
faq.answer: Redemptions in an evergreen fund can be limited or gated during periods of high demand, meaning you may not get back the full amount you request when you request it. This is a structural feature of the fund, and it is worth understanding before committing capital you may need on short notice.

faq.question: Why would a fund choose an evergreen structure instead of a fixed term?
faq.answer: An evergreen structure lets a fund continue investing and reinvesting proceeds without being forced to sell assets on a fixed timeline. This can suit strategies built around long holding periods, though it also means investors give up the certainty of a scheduled return of capital.

faq.question: Are evergreen funds regulated the same way as mutual funds?
faq.answer: Evergreen funds can be structured under different regulatory frameworks depending on how they are offered and who they are sold to. Some operate under rules similar to interval funds, while others are offered privately with different disclosure and eligibility requirements.

faq.question: How do fees in an evergreen fund compare to a traditional closed-end fund?
faq.answer: Both structures commonly charge a management fee and often a performance fee on gains. The specific rates and calculation methods vary fund by fund, so comparing fee structures directly requires reading each fund's offering documents.

what-is-an-evergreen-fund.closing: Evergreen funds offer a different tradeoff between liquidity, structure, and time horizon than traditional private or public funds. Given the complexity involved, ask your advisor whether this fits your situation.
